messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer INC-8476: tool/function-call args arriving as truncated JSON when we stream responses. They see schema validation errors from the tool because the args field is cut mid-object.

alex: Minimal repro attached below — streaming the tool call with a ~5KB args payload, result on their side: "Unexpected end of JSON input".

alex: Raw server->client SSE sample we captured:
```
data: {
data:  "tool": "search", "args": {"q": "first chunk text..."}

data: {"args_cont": "...rest of text with closing braces"}
```

support-bot: Created ticket RED-8476, priority P1. Assigned to @maya. :white_check_mark:

maya: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl or client code that reproduces? Also which edge/proxy is in front of the customer?

alex: Repro curl (customer used node fetch but curl mimics):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"x","messages":[],"tool_call":{"name":"search","args":<big JSON>}}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate
```
They also routed through an internal nginx reverse proxy at their infra boundary.

julian: Hypothesis: proxy (or client TCP stack) is splitting SSE chunks mid-JSON string. If we emit raw SSE lines without framing guarantee, a 4KB buffer boundary can cut inside a UTF-8 string, producing two SSE events that each look like partial JSON. Our runtime assumes each SSE event is a full JSON blob for tool args.

julian: Quick evidence from captured bytes — we see a chunk boundary right after a "...text part 4096 chars":
```
..."q": "...long text (4096 bytes)

// next TCP chunk
continued text finishing JSON"} }
```

sophie: +1 nginx. Default proxy_buffers are small and chunked transfer will split upstream writes. If the client or intermediary doesn't reassemble properly, the consumer sees partial SSE events. We've seen this before with multipart streaming.

maya: Customer cannot touch their proxy. They want a fix on our side. Suggested short-term mitigations?

julian: Short term: server-side reassembly in the runtime. Instead of treating each SSE 'data:' emission as a complete JSON, buffer consecutive data lines until we can successfully JSON.parse the concatenation. Pseudo: 
```js
let buf = '';
onSSEData(line){
  buf += line;
  try{ JSON.parse(buf); emit(JSON.parse(buf)); buf = ''; }
  catch(e){ /* wait for more data */ }
}
```
This will handle chunk-splits without relying on client reassembly.

sophie: That approach is safe; we should also add a length-prefixed framing detector as fallback. If our runtime sees an event header like "len: ####" we can pre-allocate and wait for exact bytes.

julian: I'll add a defensive parser + unit tests that simulate chunk boundaries at random offsets. Will instrument metrics for "partial-json-repairs" so we can see frequency.

maya: For immediate mitigation for INC-8476, can we toggle non-streaming (single response) for their API key so their tool call args arrive intact? That avoids SSE chunking entirely.

alex: Yes please — customer agrees to a temporary fallback. Their production latency tolerates it.

sophie: I'll add a temporary routing rule to disable streaming for that key and update the customer. Config change: set route header X-Redwood-Stream: false for that API key.

maya: Action items:
- maya: enable non-streaming fallback for INC-8476 and confirm with customer.
- julian: implement defensive SSE assembler + tests (+ metric) — target patch in next patch window.
- sophie: create an infra playbook note about proxy buffer tuning (proxy_buffers 8 32k / proxy_buffer_size 32k) and monitor for similar customers.

julian: Quick follow-up — adding the assembler will also handle other cases like intermediate proxies that re-chunk by MTU. Implementation note: keep it bounded (max 1MB) and drop with error if we never close the JSON after N seconds.

alex: Customer updated: temporary fallback accepted. I'll keep them posted when patch lands. Thanks all. :pray:

support-bot: RED-8476 updated: fallback enabled; pending runtime patch.

maya: I'll close the loop after we ship the runtime fix and confirm no regressions in canary. :eyes:
